historical_references.reference: The legend of Saint Christa or Christina the Astonishing was born in 1150 in the town of Seille, near the town of Huy, in the present-day Belgium. She is said to have lived a life of extreme asceticism, subjecting herself to various mortifications and performing miracles, including surviving under water for hours and walking on the frozen Meuse river. She died in 1224, enclosed in a cell she had built for herself.

Christa (or Christine) of Venice, a Christian martyr, was born in 1213 in Venice, Italy. She renounced her wealthy family to follow Christ, and was persecuted for her faith during the period of the Latin Empire in Constantinople (1204-1261). She was tortured and beheaded in 1222, and is now venerated as a saint in both the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches.
